decision.about: how the assistant preset supplies its persona and resumes its session

options.say: system prompt, a fresh session every message
system prompt, one resumed session per browser tab
the persona as the first user message instead, fresh every time

decision.because: measured first-chunk time is about the same for system-prompt and first-message (roughly 2.3 to 4.2s either way, n=3, small sample) so latency does not pick a winner -- but system-prompt injection is architecturally simpler: the exact same --append-system-prompt call works unchanged whether the turn is the first message of a tab or the fiftieth, while first-message mode would need the caller to remember whether the persona was already said in this session. Resumed vs fresh is the real win: a fresh session paid two of three runs at 17 to 22 seconds TOTAL (the CLI cold-starting hooks and MCP servers each time) while every resumed run finished in 4 to 8.5 seconds total, so the server storing one session id per browser tab (Assistant.js) is what the numbers actually favor.
decision.rule: code#1 (less is more -- fewer moving parts) plus the measured numbers in this same log line above

decision.about: should a closed browser tab kill its in-flight claude -p turn

options.say: leave it as today: the turn always finishes and records, tab open or not
kill the child for every ask(), streaming or not, the instant its socket closes
kill the child only for STREAMING turns; a plain ask() keeps finishing and recording

decision.because: the prove step asks for a closed tab to kill the child, and nothing in Ask.js did that before this task -- it is a real gap, not pre-existing behavior. But killing EVERY turn on tab-close would change chat.js and the dev rail thread panel today: a browser tab closed mid-reply currently still finishes and files the exchange into that task task.jsonl, which is reasonable (the owner may reopen the tab and expect the answer). Streaming exists only to paint a live tab, so a gone tab leaves it no reason to keep running -- scoping the kill to stream:true turns gets the proof its behavior with zero change to the existing chat path.
decision.rule: code#1 less is more -- the smallest change that satisfies the ask without touching a working path

log.msg: First real proof run (headless Playwright, port 8142) caught a genuine bug: the assistant reply on screen started with reading the state... even though the preset passes tools: empty string. Cause: tools: empty string only disables the BUILT-IN tool set -- the .mcp.json site MCP server still reaches every headless turn regardless, so the model opened a tool_use block anyway. Fixed by adding --strict-mcp-config (no --mcp-config of its own) to the assistant preset, confirmed with a scratch run showing mcp_servers: [] and tools: [] in the turn own system/init event. Ask.js args() gained a strict_mcp option; Assistant.preset() now sets it.

All four Prove requirements passed, headless Playwright against the private port-8142 server. (1) first chunk in DOM at 1680ms, turn done at 2991ms (first before done), reply grew across 3+ distinct-length observations, rpc-path text and tailed-board text were byte-identical, zero console errors. (2) owner + assistant card lines and chunk lines landed correctly in scratch-board.jsonl (never board.jsonl), and the relay landed correctly in scratch-ledger.jsonl (never a real task.jsonl) for every test message sent. (3) two messages from the same tab: both ask_done events carried the exact same session_id (2c986e38-...), confirming the per-tab resume in Assistant.js works. (4) closed-tab-kills-child: a new claude.exe pid (38888) appeared during a turn and was confirmed GONE from the process list 1.5s after page.close() -- the kill-on-close fix in Ask.js turn() works. One real bug found and fixed along the way: tools: empty-string does not disable MCP-supplied tools (only built-in ones), so the assistant preset was opening a stray tool_use block against the site MCP server; fixed with --strict-mcp-config.

assign.outcome:
**The assistant's reply now types itself out on the owner's screen, word by word, as the model writes it — proved live, not just built.** `claude -p --include-partial-messages` carries text deltas; the server forwards each one over the socket as an append-only `ask_chunk`, then one `ask_done` with both timings. A new `assistant` preset (Sonnet, `--effort low`, no tools at all — `tools: ""` plus `--strict-mcp-config`, a real bug this caught: `tools: ""` alone left the `site` MCP server reachable) runs as one session resumed per browser tab, and the SERVER — not the model — writes the owner's words and the growing/finished reply to the shared board (`card`/`chunk` lines, batched every ~150ms or 40 chars) and relays the words to the mastermind's inbox.

**The numbers.** Time to first word on screen (n=3, tiny prompts): Sonnet ≈3.3s, Haiku ≈7.1s, persona-as-system-prompt and persona-as-first-message tie (~3.1–3.3s) — but a FRESH session paid 17–22s total twice out of three runs against 4–8.5s for a RESUMED one. Recommended default (shipped): **Sonnet, persona as a system prompt, one session resumed per tab.**

**The doorbell.** Yes — a headless turn given only the `SendMessage` tool successfully rang the real running mastermind session (`{success:true}`). The shipped preset still relays through the inbox file instead, because the server already does it at zero extra cost and it does not depend on which session is the mastermind's right now.

**Proved headless, private server, port 8142, SCRATCH board + ledger (never the real ones):** first chunk in the DOM before the turn ended and text grew across 3+ observations; the rpc-path text and the tailed-board text came out byte-identical; two messages from one tab resumed the exact same `session_id`; a closed tab killed its own spawned `claude.exe` within 1.5s (new — nothing tied a turn to its socket before this task, scoped to streaming turns only so `chat.js`'s existing behaviour is untouched).

**Three lines for the dev-bar composer** (the sibling building `dev/DevBar/**` / `ai/v/**`):
```js
import { stream, typewriter } from "/framework/ext/Ask/stream.js";
const view = typewriter($replyBox.el);
stream({ preset: "assistant", prompt, on_chunk: e => view.chunk(e.text), on_done: e => view.done() });
```
The owner's words and the reply already land on the shared board from the server, so the composer's own board reader shows the conversation with no other wiring.

**Needs the owner:** nothing new — this never touched the owner's port-80 server; everything above ran on a private port-8142 instance and against scratch files.
